svg.aria-label: Schematic example of CR scheduling with max_parallel_ops 4. Panel 1: five MUXes; MUX n holds qubits 4n to 4n plus 3. Eight selected directed pairs, drawn as arrows from control to target and colored and tagged by their execution group: 0 to 1, 3 to 1 and 3 to 2 in MUX0, 4 to 5 in MUX1, 8 to 9 in MUX2, 12 to 13 in MUX3, 16 to 17 in MUX4, and the inter-MUX pair 7 to 10. Each MUX has its own readout module; MUX1 and MUX2 share control module C1. Panel 2: the conflict graph has one node per pair, drawn without group colors. 0 to 1 and 3 to 1 conflict because they share qubit 1; 3 to 1 and 3 to 2 share qubit 3; 0 to 1 and 3 to 2 use the same MUX0; 4 to 5 and 8 to 9 use MUXes that share control module C1. 12 to 13 and 16 to 17 have no conflict. The inter-MUX pair 7 to 10 is colored in a separate graph. Greedy coloring gives graph color 1 to 0 to 1, 4 to 5, 12 to 13 and 16 to 17, graph color 2 to 3 to 1 and 8 to 9, and graph color 3 to 3 to 2; 7 to 10 gets color 1 of the inter-MUX graph. Panel 3, execution groups, each with its own color: blue G1 holds the four pairs 0 to 1, 4 to 5, 12 to 13 and 16 to 17; orange G2 holds 3 to 1 and 8 to 9; teal G3 holds 3 to 2; purple G4, the only inter-MUX group, holds 7 to 10. Groups run in order from G1 to G4.

g.text: Selected CR pairs on a schematic wiring
Arrows point from control to target; color and tag give the execution group from panel 3.
R: readout module. C: control module. Module names are illustrative.
Conflict graph: one node per pair, one edge per conflict
Edges are scheduling conflicts, not couplings. Linked nodes get different graph colors, written as text.
Execution groups (max_parallel_ops = 4), run left to right
Each graph color fits in one group, so G1 runs four pairs at once. A cap of 2 would split G1 in two.
